signals.title: VTSTech/AgentKthx
signals.content: ⚛️ AgentKthx - minimal, modular, python stdlib, agentic framework for tool calling AI agents. Runs locally with Ollama, BitNet, TurboQuant, in the cloud with OpenRouter, ZAI, HuggingFace, and Google Gemini. Extensible via a manifest-based plugin system for additional backends and features.
signals.score_reason: high-value open-source ecosystem signal; agentic AI relevance. Final score: 70. Freshness: source age 0d.
signals.brief_en: VTSTech/AgentKthx – A lightweight, modular Python framework built on the standard library for creating agentic AI tools. It supports local execution with Ollama, BitNet, and TurboQuant, and cloud deployment via OpenRouter, ZAI, HuggingFace, and Google Gemini. Extensibility is provided through a manifest‑based plugin system that allows additional backends and features to be integrated. The design emphasizes minimal dependencies, ease of integration, and flexible tool‑calling capabilities.
signals.brief_ar: VTSTech/AgentKthx – إطار عمل خفيف الوزن ومُجزَّأ بلغة بايثون يعتمد على مكتبة اللغة القياسية لإنشاء وكلاء ذكاء اصطناعي قادرين على استدعاء الأدوات. يدعم التنفيذ المحلي عبر Ollama وBitNet وTurboQuant، والنشر السحابي عبر OpenRouter وZAI وHuggingFace وGoogle Gemini. يُمكن توسيعه عبر نظام إضافات قائم على ملفات التعريف (manifest) لإضافة خلفيات وخدمات جديدة. يركز التصميم على تقليل الاعتماديات، سهولة التكامل، وقدرات استدعاء الأدوات المرنة.

signals.brief_en: shurrey/illuminate-poc-backend: A FERPA-compliant multi-agent AI framework for natural language querying of educational data. It integrates AWS Bedrock AgentCore (A2A protocol), Claude, and Snowflake to generate SQL-backed responses and interactive visualizations via a React/CloudFront frontend.

signals.score_reason: high-value open-source ecosystem signal; agentic AI relevance; retrieval/RAG relevance. Final score: 52. Freshness: source age 0d.
signals.brief_en:
Title: BitConcepts/glossa-lab

An agentic computational linguistics platform delivering OSINT‑grade analysis of ancient scripts. Current capabilities include processing the Indus Script with 161 H+M proto‑Dravidian readings, achieving 90.96% token coverage and applying a three‑slot positional grammar (z=10.3). The system supports AI‑assisted corpus analysis, hypothesis testing, and literature discovery, and is released as open‑source software.
